subject: Risk & Compliance
title: The US-China Trade War
description: A quick, practical guide to The US-China Trade War.

hook.text: In 2018, the US imposed tariffs on $250 billion in Chinese goods. China retaliated instantly. A trade war began.

buildup.text: The trade war targeted technology, agriculture, and manufacturing, disrupting supply chains across both countries.

discovery.text: US farmers lost $27 billion in exports. Chinese manufacturers relocated to Vietnam and Mexico to avoid tariffs.

twist.text: The trade war accelerated US-China decoupling — a strategic separation that may reshape global trade for decades.

climax.text: Trade wars create losers on both sides. But geopolitical goals sometimes outweigh economic costs.

punchline.text: $250 billion in tariffs. Both sides lost. Decoupling accelerated.

quiz.question: What was a major consequence of the US-China trade war?
options: Accelerated strategic decoupling between the two economies
Both countries became more economically integrated
